textbookText: 137. Kinetic theory predicts that at very high pressure, real gases deviate from ideal behavior mainly because: A) The finite volume of molecules becomes significant relative to the container volume (violating the point-mass assumption) B) Molecular collisions become perfectly elastic only at high pressure C) Temperature automatically drops to zero D) Molecules stop moving entirely

138. Kinetic theory predicts that at very low temperature, real gases deviate from ideal behavior mainly because: A) Intermolecular attractive forces become significant as molecular speeds decrease, leading toward liquefaction B) Molecules move faster, increasing collision frequency infinitely C) The gas constant R changes value D) Pressure automatically becomes zero

139. The mean free path of a gas molecule is defined as: A) The average distance travelled by a molecule between successive collisions B) The total distance travelled by a molecule in one second C) The diameter of the gas molecule D) The distance between the container walls

140. Which factor increases the mean free path of gas molecules? A) Decreasing the pressure (fewer molecules per unit volume, so fewer collisions) B) Increasing the pressure C) Increasing the number of molecules at constant volume D) Decreasing the temperature at constant volume

141. According to kinetic theory, why does a gas exert equal pressure in all directions on its container? A) Because molecular motion is completely random and isotropic (no preferred direction) B) Because gravity pulls molecules only downward C) Because molecules move only along straight horizontal paths D) Because pressure is defined only at the container's base

142. Kinetic theory's assumption that the actual volume of gas molecules is negligible compared to the total volume of the gas holds best under conditions of: A) Low pressure and high temperature B) High pressure and low temperature C) STP conditions strictly and only D) Any pressure and temperature, without exception
143. The relationship between average kinetic energy (KE) per molecule and absolute temperature is: A) KE = (3/2)kT, where k is the Boltzmann constant B) KE = kT² C) KE = 3kT² D) KE = k/T

144. Which gas, at a given temperature, would have the highest rms speed among H₂, O₂, N₂, and CO₂ (based on kinetic theory)? A) H₂ (lowest molar mass gives highest rms speed) B) O₂ C) N₂ D) CO₂ (highest molar mass gives lowest rms speed)

145. Kinetic theory explains Charles's law (V ∝ T at constant P) by reasoning that increased temperature: A) Increases molecular speed/collision force, requiring greater volume to keep pressure constant B) Decreases the number of molecules C) Has no effect on molecular motion D) Only affects the container material, not the gas

146. An extraordinary application of kinetic theory of gases is in explaining: A) Why hot air balloons rise — heated air has faster-moving, more widely spaced molecules, lowering its density relative to cooler surrounding air B) Why solids conduct electricity C) Why liquids have a fixed shape D) Why chemical bonds form between atoms

147. Kinetic theory assumes molecular collisions and motion between collisions are: A) Random in direction but obey Newton's laws of motion in straight-line paths between collisions B) Always curved paths under a central force C) Completely predictable in exact direction for each molecule D) Governed by chemical attraction, not physics

148. The postulate of kinetic theory most directly responsible for explaining why gases have low density compared to liquids/solids is: A) Large intermolecular spacing with molecules occupying negligible volume relative to total gas volume B) Perfectly elastic collisions C) Random molecular motion in all directions D) Equal average kinetic energy at a given temperature

149. According to kinetic theory, pressure of an ideal gas can be expressed as P = (1/3)ρc̄², where ρ is density and c̄² is: A) The mean square speed of the gas molecules B) The mean free path C) The molar mass D) The number of molecules

150. Kinetic theory's core achievement was to: A) Provide a molecular-level (microscopic) explanation for macroscopically observed gas laws and thermal behavior B) Disprove all previously established gas laws C) Explain only liquid behavior, not gases D) Replace the need for the ideal gas equation entirely
